what: ANIMATION [the PC playtest: the bodies' part], rule 164 item 31 (Paolo 10/24 on his PC: more and better animations when people hold things), the coordinator's order 10/25: (1) melee weapons held right in the hand, idle, walk, the swing, the hit taken; (2) the shield arm; (3) anything else held in the wrong pose. THE KEPT SOURCE (rule 128) of tools/bohemia_animation_melee_in_hand.py: the new keys on the rig's man (the same step grammar as records/target/animation/BOHEMIA_WHAT_A_MAN_HOLDS.json, whose parts these lists may name), the props, which Battle Brothers row holds which prop, and on which keys of which clip a prop is rendered in his hand.

MIdleX.why: the melee idle's own keys (the club tapped into the left palm, the club laid on the right shoulder); its rest, breath and looks are the pistol's (PIdle keys 0 to 3, the same right arm at the one-hand low ready), so they are never rendered twice

SIdle.why: the shield carried on the left forearm across his front, his right hand at the one-hand low ready (a club or a pistol in it); a breath, a look each way

SWalk.why: the walk's six keys with the shield held across him and the right hand low: neither arm swings

SSwing.why: COMBAT's own swing (its Swing turns of the right arm and the chest, tools/bohemia_combat_the_fight_poses.py man_keys) with the shield kept up on the left arm

SAim.why: the pistol out at the eye in one hand over the shield, the shield up at the guard (never bladed: the shield stays in front)

SBlock.why: THE BLOCK: a blow lands and the shield is up before his face, he leans into it; then he is rocked behind it

SCover.why: on one knee behind the cover with the shield planted on the ground before him, the thing in his right hand up at his chest; a breath; a peek

SCoverHit.why: on the knee behind the shield, rocked

T2Idle.why: a two-handed thing held across him in both hands at COMBAT's low ready (the long gun's carry), a breath, a look each way; THE LEAN: its head set down on the ground before him and both hands stacked on the end of the haft

T2Swing.why: the two-handed blow: both hands on the haft raised over his right shoulder; brought down before him, his right hand ahead of and below his left so the head lands forward and down; followed through low to his left

BIdle.why: the bow held low in his LEFT fist before his hip, its limbs up and down, his right hand free: a breath, a look each way

BShot.why: THE DRAW AND THE LOOSE (the coordinator's 10/26 item (3): 'the bows' poses'): the bow comes up before him with his right hand on the string; then bladed, his left shoulder to the mark, the bow arm straight out at shoulder height and the string hand at his jaw, his head turned back over the bow arm to look down the arrow; then the loose, the string hand flying back past his ear

composite.why: a melee clip as the fight plays it, key by key, from the clip a key was rendered on: the held sheets' PIdle, PCarryWalk, PHit, CoverPistol, CoverHit (last round's, slices/rig_hold), this source's MIdleX (slices/rig_melee), and COMBAT's own Swing on the fight sheet (slices/fight_rig); the prop is rendered in his hand on every one

hold.why: how the prop sits in his right fist on each key: rest, along the forearm at the one-hand low ready, the head up and forward; tap, the head in his left palm; tap_lift, the head lifted a hand off it; shoulder, laid back over his right shoulder; wind, cocked back behind his head; blow and follow, in line with the forearm; hit, kept in the fist as he is rocked; port, up before his chest on one knee

pipe.say: a length of rusted water pipe with a coupling at each end and tape at the grip (the thug's pipe, COOK THREE's tier)

club.say: a table leg turned into a club, faceted, heavier at the far end, the grip wound in tape

bat.say: an ash baseball bat with nails driven through the barrel (Battle Brothers' morning star in the valley's hands)

cleaver.say: a butcher's cleaver: a wooden grip, a deep square blade, the edge ground bright

machete.say: a machete: a black grip, a long flat blade with a belly toward the tip and a rust patch (the market's BLADE)

hatchet.say: the poacher's hatchet: a short wooden haft, a bearded steel head, the edge ground bright

pistol.say: COOK's pistol (reference/models/bohemia/gun_pistol_a.glb), the gun every pistol man holds

car_door.say: a car door cut off below the window: the faded skin, a dent and bullet holes, rust at the seams, the handle, the window channel's two stubs, a strap behind

crash_bar.say: the Heavy's crash-bar shield (CHARACTER's): a rounded frame of steel tube, a diamond-plate panel, the bent push bar, a dead plate riveted on

sledge.say: a sledgehammer: a long taped haft, a steel head with bright faces

rebar_spear.say: COOK's rebar spear; until it lands, a stand-in: a sign post's pipe and a leaf of spring steel lashed on with wire, a rag under it

chain.say: COOK's chain (the flails); until it lands, a stand-in: a handle, a chain that hangs and trails the swing, a spiked ball

bottles.say: COOK's bottles (the thrown things); until they land, COOK's own Molotov from the market icon at its real size

fire_axe.say: COOK's fire axe (the axes); until it lands, a stand-in felling axe

pole_hook.say: COOK's pole hook (the polearms, the pitchfork); until it lands, a stand-in pitchfork

riot_shield.say: COOK's riot shield (the market's name for every shield of durability 40 or more)

compound_bow.say: COOK's compound bow (reference/models/bohemia/item_compound_bow.glb, the eight bow rows of its table), held in his LEFT fist: the grip at the origin, the limbs up and down, the arrow forward

sling.say: a herder's sling (the armoury's staff sling and nomad sling, COOK's table gives them its thrown bottles): two braided cords from his fist to a leather pouch with a stone in it; hangs from his fist, whirled out behind him on the wind, flung out before him on the loose. This tool's stand-in until COOK models one

pool_pole_spear.say: COOK's the pool pole spear (rule 337): a pool skimmer pole, its teal cam-lock collar, a kitchen knife taped into the clip end

extension_cord.say: COOK's the extension cord (rule 337): an orange garage cord wound round his fist, the rest hanging to its three-prong plug

live_wire.say: COOK's the live wire (rule 337): a drill battery taped on a pipe stub for a handle, a switch, black cable to its stripped copper end

barbed_wire.say: COOK's the barbed wire (rule 337): a taped broom stub, a rope tied on, two strands of rusted barbed wire twisted onto the rope

rodeo_bullwhip.say: COOK's the rodeo bullwhip (rule 337): a plaited leather bullwhip, its wrist loop and brass ring, the thong down to the fall and the cracker

crowbar.say: COOK's the crowbar (rule 337): a red wrecking bar gone to bare steel where it is held, the gooseneck claw, the flat chisel at the butt

bike_lock_chain.say: COOK's the bike-lock chain (rule 337): a square-link bike chain in its torn black sleeve, bunched and taped for a grip, the lock barrel with its key

box_cutter.say: COOK's the box cutter (rule 337): a yellow heavy-duty utility knife, the blade run all the way out, the body wound in black tape

framing_hammer.say: COOK's the framing hammer (rule 337): a hickory framing hammer, the milled face, the straight rip claw with a bent nail caught in it

broom_bayonet.say: COOK's the broom bayonet (rule 337): a painted broom handle, an old bayonet hose-clamped to its end, the paint worn to wood at the grip

pawn_shop_katana.say: COOK's the pawn-shop katana (rule 337): a wall-hanger katana, its wrapped grip, the round guard, the pawn tag still tied on its string

splitting_maul.say: COOK's the splitting maul (rule 337): an eight-pound maul, the wedge ground bright, the sledge face behind it, the red paint mostly gone

sign_post_halberd.say: COOK's the sign-post halberd (rule 337): a punched steel sign post, a STOP sign cut into an axe blade and bolted on, the post cut to a spike

by_row.why: every one-handed row of the armoury to the thing COOK's table makes of it (records/target/cook_every_item/BOHEMIA_EVERY_ITEM_AND_ITS_MODEL.json; rule 177: what you equip is what you see): the market's thing is the fight's

by_class.why: a row COOK's table does not name falls back on its class

timelines.why: as the held clips: slots of two bars (24 keys); an even slot a breath, an odd slot one of the rest rolled off his own seed: the look each way, THE TAP (the club head lifted off his left palm and brought down into it three times, on the beat's thirds), THE SHOULDER (the club laid on his right shoulder for a bar); every slot starts and ends on key 0 and a big move passes a half key

shield_hold.why: how the shield sits on his left forearm: carry, across his front turned a little to his left flank; guard, the same a hand higher; block, square before his face; low, planted on the ground before him on one knee

shield_by_row.why: every shield row to COOK's thing (the wooden and the small ones a car door, the Heavy's metal one the crash bar, the tall metal ones a riot shield)

shield_over.why: which is drawn last where the thing in his right hand and the shield on his left cross: the shield, but where his right side is toward the glass (SE, E, NE)

hold_by_prop.why: a short blade or a hatchet laid back on the shoulder goes behind a collar, a hood or a fur hat (measured: the cleaver hidden in 3 to 5 facings on the blues, the caravans and the church, the hatchet in 5 on the blues): it is held up beside his head instead; the cleaver's tap is the flat lifted off his palm (tapped down into a fur coat's front it is gone in 5 facings, the caravans)

two_by_row.why: every two-handed row to COOK's thing for it, held in both hands

two_by_class.why: a two-handed row COOK's table does not name falls back on its class

props_from.why: measured 10/25: with the scale his model renders at within 0.006 of YOU's (1.101 to 1.110), a look's things on the held keys differ from YOU's by about one pixel at the edges (17 to 28 px of a thing's 88 differ, the order of a one-pixel shift of a thin haft; his rolled men already hold their gang's things on their own bodies the same way), so these twenty hold YOU's things past the first layer, moved by the difference of their feet. The rest render their own: a hat that makes the man taller makes him smaller in the frame (the wide brim 1.054, the caravans 1.058, 105 and 110 px of 88 off), and the anarchists, the church and the network sit two pixels off (29 to 44); the two tiers are their own build. About five hours of renders saved. AMENDED 10/25 later the same round: COOK shipped its 24 models, so every look's own things would be drawn again; laid on their own bodies and checked by the gate's touch leg (H1: wherever the thing shows it is within 2 px of his body, on every key and facing), YOU's things hold in the anarchists', the church's and the network's fists too (two pixels off in scale) and in the first layer for all twenty-three, so they hold YOU's from the first layer; only the caravans and the wide brim (a hat that makes them smaller in the frame, 105 to 110 px off) and the two tiers (COOK THREE's thug and poacher, whose models carry their own weapon) draw their own.

cook_models.why: a thing whose COOK model is in the folder is rendered from it (COOK builds them in this tool's frame, rule 177(c)); the stand-ins in tools/bohemia_animation_melee_in_hand.py hold only until then, and a man's thing is rendered again the moment its model changes (props/models.json)

bow_by_class.why: a bow is drawn and loosed in its own keys (BIdle, BShot): every row of the bow class (COOK's table: its compound bow)

sling_by_row.why: the slings are whirled, not thrown as a bottle: drawn as the sling once its layer (m3) is live, as the bottle until then

withhold.why: a named look whose shield arm is not right yet keeps his one-hand stance in the fight (his shield's pictures left out by the pack): the thug's and the poacher's planted shields, measured 10/26 by THE THING IN HIS HAND G1, sink 14 to 15 px facing west and float 5 px facing east (their bigger build kneels deeper: pulled in to PLANT_REACH his front leg hides the shield's foot in profile), and the poacher's block tops out a pixel low; the next round's placement; the caravans and the wide brim (10/26): measured from the top of their hats, the crash bar's block tops out 27 and 28 px under it and the pipe's two-handed wind 6 px under it, and the caravans' pistol with the shield shows in 92 of 144 pictures (64 percent): their shield arm and two hands held back until a look at what a hat does to the crown COOK 11/3: a look whose shield arm or two hands are held back holds them back on the new layers too (s4, t4), and the list rides in his json ('withhold') so his things borrowed from YOU's sheet (props_ref) skip those layers.

every_weapon_its_own: COOK 11/3 (rule 337, ask line 344, tools/bohemia_cook_every_weapon_its_own_11_3_26.py): the armory's pieces were drawn as their family's model; each is its own model now, rendered in YOU's hands on the new layers m4 (one hand), s4 (one hand with a shield) and t4 (two hands), and every other man holds YOU's pictures moved by the difference of their feet (props_ref). 'hanging': the things whose cord, thong or chain hangs from the handle's end and trails the swing (build_prop).
